1	# Nova — Sprint 8 Competitor Benchmark: Artists / Team / Scheduling
2	
3	**Target:** InkOS — multi-user tattoo studio SaaS. Scope: staff artists, guest artists, shift grids, time-off, invites, permissions matrix.
4	**Benchmarked:** Rippling (HR/IT), Gusto (people/payroll), Linear (team pages), Notion (membership), Fresha + Mindbody (beauty scheduling), Porter/Mangomint (tattoo-specific).
5	
6	---
7	
8	## Part 1 — Team Member Roster
9	
10	### List view pattern
11	- **Rippling** uses a dense **table** (avatar, name, role, department, status, start date, manager). Virtualized, multi-column sort, saved views. Best for 50+ members.
12	- **Linear** uses a **hybrid table** — avatar + name + email + role column + joined date + last active. Sparse density, no specialty chips. Good reference for ≤30 members.
13	- **Gusto** uses a **card grid on mobile, table on desktop**. Card shows avatar, name, role, compensation summary on hover.
14	- **Fresha** uses **vertical cards with color accent** (artist's assigned calendar color) — works because beauty studios are small (5–15 team members).
15	
16	**InkOS recommendation:** Table view primary (like Rippling) because studios hit 10–25 members with commissions. Add a **toggle** to "Cards" for smaller studios or mobile. Columns: Avatar · Name · Role (chip) · Specialty (chip list) · Status · Commission % · Next shift · Actions.
17	
18	### Filters
19	- Rippling uses **filter chips above the table** (Role, Status, Department, Location, Manager) with a "+ Add filter" button for custom fields.
20	- Linear uses **a single search bar + role dropdown**. Under-powered for InkOS.
21	- **InkOS filters:** Role (Owner/Artist/Receptionist/Guest), Status (Active/Inactive/Pending invite/On leave), Specialty (Black & Grey / Color / Realism / Traditional / Piercing), Availability today (toggle).
22	
23	### Profile page
24	Strongest template is **Gusto's employee profile**: left rail with avatar + name + role + "Message" CTA; right pane with tabs (Overview, Compensation, Time Off, Documents, Notes).
25	
26	**InkOS artist profile tabs:**
27	1. **Overview** — hero (avatar + name + role + status + specialties + Instagram link); stats grid (appointments this month, revenue YTD, avg rating, no-show rate, commission earned MTD)
28	2. **Schedule** — mini week view, next 5 bookings
29	3. **Portfolio** — 3×3 photo grid (most recent tattoo photos from completed bookings — auto-populated from client session photos with artist tag, gated by consent)
30	4. **Commission & Payroll** — current rate, YTD earnings, next payout
31	5. **Documents** — contractor agreement, W-9, licenses, insurance
32	6. **Permissions** — read-only view of their role + link to edit
33	
34	### Portfolio/examples
35	Fresha shows artist photos as **a horizontal carousel under the profile header** — this is the strongest pattern for a scheduling-heavy tool because the user lands for scheduling but sees portfolio instantly. Mangomint uses a dedicated "Portfolio" tab. Notion/Linear don't ship this. Copy Fresha carousel + Mangomint tab separation.
36	
37	---
38	
39	## Part 2 — Shift Scheduling Grid
40	
41	### Grid layout
42	- **Fresha** — **artists as columns (vertical), time as rows**. Day view default, week view as toggle. 15-min slot granularity. Colored blocks span time ranges. Drag edges to extend. Drag block body to reassign artist or move time.
43	- **Mindbody** — same vertical-columns layout, but week view shows **multi-day resource schedule** (each artist gets a sub-column per day).
44	- **Rippling** — **horizontal rows = people, columns = days**, designed for shift blocks not appointments. Simpler, less granular (no 15-min slots).
45	
46	**InkOS recommendation:** **Fresha-style vertical artist columns + time rows** for the day view (this is where bookings happen). Add a **"Shift schedule" toggle** that flips to Rippling-style horizontal rows × days for weekly shift planning (no appointments, just availability windows). Two modes, one grid component.
47	
48	### Drag-assign
49	Fresha's drag model is the gold standard — click-hold a booking block → drag vertically to change time, drag horizontally to change artist. Ghost preview shows new slot before commit. **Must-have for InkOS.**
50	
51	Rippling's shift assignment uses a simpler **"click empty cell → pick shift template → apply"** flow. Copy this for empty-shift creation; use Fresha's drag for moving.
52	
53	### Templates
54	- Fresha — **"Working hours templates"** saved per artist (e.g. "Tuesday–Saturday 11am–8pm"). Apply on hire.
55	- Rippling — **"Shift patterns"** at team level; assign patterns to employees.
56	- **InkOS:** Per-artist default template (their weekly availability) + per-studio "week template" (staffing pattern: how many artists on each day/shift). One-click "Apply template to next 4 weeks".
57	
58	### Copy previous week
59	Rippling and Mindbody both ship **"Copy from last week"** as a single button in the week header. Fresha has **"Duplicate week"** in the overflow menu. Put this button front-and-center in InkOS — studios are repetitive.
60

# Nova — Sprint 9 Competitor Benchmark: Money Flows (Payments / Commissions / Payroll / Billing)

**Target:** InkOS multi-tenant tattoo studio SaaS. Scope: payments list + refunds, commission rules/records/disputes, payroll runs with tax forms, tenant-facing billing, admin-facing MRR/churn dashboard.
**Benchmarked:** Stripe Dashboard (dashboard.stripe.com), QuickBooks Online, Pilot.com, Gusto, Rippling, Mercury (mercury.com), ProfitWell/Baremetrics (admin MRR references).

---

## Part 1 — Payment List

### Columns (Stripe Dashboard is the gold standard)
Stripe's Payments table: **Amount · Status (chip) · Description · Customer · Date · Payment method (brand + last 4) · Actions (·••)**. Sticky first column (amount), right-aligned currency, monospaced amount font, status as colored dot + text (`succeeded` green, `refunded` gray, `disputed` red, `pending` amber). [Source: dashboard.stripe.com/payments]

Mercury's Transactions table drops "Description" and adds **Counterparty** + **Category** — cleaner for banking context but less useful for us. QuickBooks adds **Memo** and **Class** columns — too accounting-heavy.

**InkOS columns:** Amount · Status · Client · Artist · Booking / Service · Method (Card/Cash/Zelle/Cashapp) · Date · Actions. Monospace amount. Tabular-nums on dates. Click row → opens drawer (not page — Stripe pattern).

### Filter drawer
Stripe uses a **right-side slide-in drawer** with sections: Date range (preset pills + custom), Status (multi-checkbox), Amount (min/max), Payment method, Currency, Customer search. "Clear all" + "Apply" sticky footer. Saved views across top of table ("All", "Succeeded today", "Refunded this month"). [Source: stripe.com/docs/dashboard]

Mercury uses **inline filter chips** above table — simpler but caps out at ~5 filters.

**InkOS:** Copy Stripe's drawer pattern exactly. Sections: Date range, Status, Amount range, Method, Artist (for multi-artist studios), Client search. Saved views: "Today", "This week", "Pending deposits", "Refunds", "Disputed". Filter state persists in URL for sharing.

### Refund flow
Stripe's refund is a **modal, not a drawer**: amount field (prefilled full amount, editable for partial), reason dropdown (`duplicate`/`fraudulent`/`requested_by_customer`/`other`), internal note field, destructive red confirm button showing **"Refund $X to •••• 4242"** — the last-4 confirmation prevents mistakes. Optimistic UI flips row to `refunded` immediately, rolls back on API error. [Source: dashboard.stripe.com refund modal]

**InkOS:** Same modal. Add "Restock deposit-used inventory?" checkbox (tattoo-specific — if a needle/ink cartridge was counted against the booking). Require typed client name for full refunds >$200 (safety gate). Auto-void commission record on full refund, show "Commission of $X also reversed" inline.

### Invoice preview drawer
QuickBooks uses a **right-side drawer** with full invoice rendered as PDF preview + "Download PDF" + "Send again" + "Mark paid" buttons. Stripe shows a **hosted invoice URL** inline with a live preview iframe. [Source: quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support]

**InkOS:** Drawer with three tabs: **Preview** (rendered invoice HTML), **History** (sent/opened/paid events timeline), **Actions** (Resend · Download PDF · Edit memo · Void). Mirror Stripe's "Pay this invoice" public link for clients who can't find the email.

### Receipt resend
Stripe ships a tiny "Resend receipt" button that opens a one-field modal (email, prefilled with customer email). Success toast: "Receipt sent to foo@bar.com". No back-end drama. **Copy verbatim.** Add SMS resend option for InkOS (clients often book by phone, no email).

---

## Part 2 — Commission Rules

### Formula builder vs config
Rippling's **compensation rules** use a **config form** (not formula builder): dropdowns for "Pay type: Hourly/Salary/Commission", "Rate: %", "Applied to: Revenue/Profit/Tips". Simple, no free-form math. [Source: rippling.com/payroll]

Gusto uses **plain config + custom earnings types** — admin creates an "Earning" called "Commission" with a flat % or fixed amount. No conditional logic.

QuickBooks Payroll has a **rule builder**: IF (service category = X) THEN (commission = Y%). Closer to what InkOS needs but it's buried in settings.

**InkOS recommendation:** **Config form, not formula builder** — 90% of studios use one of three patterns: (a) flat % of service revenue, (b) tiered % (50% up to $5k/week, 60% after), (c) split (60% artist / 40% studio, supplies deducted first). Build a **preset picker** (3 cards) + "Custom tier" editor. No free-form formulas — that's Rippling's lesson: complexity deters adoption.

Config fields: Scope (per artist / studio default), Base (% of service · % of service+tip · flat $ per appointment), Deductions (supplies at cost / supplies at markup / none), Tier breakpoints (optional, up to 3 tiers), Effective date.

### Preview calculator
Pilot.com's bookkeeping rules have a **"Test this rule"** sidebar — paste a sample transaction, see computed output before saving. Stripe Tax has similar "Preview tax for example charge". [Source: pilot.com/product]

**InkOS:** Right rail **"Preview calculator"** always visible on commission rule edit page. Inputs: Service price, Tip, Supplies cost. Outputs live: Artist earns $X · Studio keeps $Y · Breakdown table (base, tip split, deductions). Updates on every keystroke. Reduces support tickets.

### Disputes comment thread
Gusto's **payroll disputes** use a **threaded comment panel** on the specific line item — artist clicks "Flag this" → modal with reason + comment → admin sees notification → reply-thread in panel (like a Notion comment thread). Resolved flag hides from default view but stays auditable. [Source: gusto.com/product/payroll]

Linear's comment pattern is the purest UI reference (threaded, markdown, @mentions).

**InkOS:** On each commission record, "View · Flag · History". Flag opens a **side panel** with: Reason dropdown (Wrong rate / Missed tip / Duplicate / Refund not applied / Other), Comment box, Attach evidence (screenshot). Admin sees unread badge in sidebar. Threaded replies. Resolution requires "Accept · Reject · Adjust" action — adjustments create a correcting entry (never edit the original — audit law).

### Leaderboard
Gusto ships a **"Top earners this period"** card on payroll dashboard. Fresha has an **artist leaderboard** widget (revenue, appointments, retention). [Source: fresha.com]

**InkOS:** Leaderboard tab on Commissions page. Columns: Rank · Artist · Services revenue · Tips · Commission earned · YoY delta. Filters: This week / month / quarter / YTD. Gamification done tastefully — medal icons for top 3, no shame for bottom. Toggle "Private mode" (owner-only) vs "Visible to all artists" (studio culture choice).

---

## Part 3 — Payroll Runs

### State machine
Gusto's payroll runs: **Draft → Review → Approve → Processing → Paid**, with **"Submit by X for pay date Y"** countdown banner. [Source: gusto.com/product/payroll] Rippling uses same states + "Correction" state for amendments.

**InkOS states:** `draft` (editable) → `review` (frozen numbers, comment-open) → `approved` (owner signed off) → `processing` (payouts initiated) → `paid` (all payouts confirmed) → `closed` (immutable, 7-year retention). Rejection from review → back to draft with reason.

### Visual stepper
Gusto uses a **horizontal stepper at top of page**: 5 dots with labels, current step filled, completed checked, future gray. Click completed steps to view read-only. [Source: gusto.com payroll run flow]

**InkOS:** Horizontal stepper (desktop), vertical on mobile. 5 steps: **1. Calculate → 2. Review → 3. Approve → 4. Pay → 5. Close**. Current step pulses (soft glow using `--color-electric-purple`). Step-blockers shown as red dot with tooltip ("2 disputes unresolved").

### Per-artist summaries
Gusto's payroll page shows **one expandable row per employee**: collapsed = name + gross + net; expanded = line items (regular hours, OT, commission, tip, pre-tax deductions, taxes, post-tax, net). [Source: gusto.com]

**InkOS:** One row per artist. Collapsed columns: Avatar · Name · Services · Commission · Tips · Gross · Deductions · **Net** (bold, monospace). Expand reveals: line-item table (all bookings), tip allocation, supplies deducted, adjustments, tax withholding (for W-2) / 1099 totals (for contractors). Inline comment thread per row.

### Tax form viewer (1099-K, W-9)
Gusto's tax forms live at `/taxes/forms` — table of forms with status (Draft / Finalized / Filed / Delivered). Click row → PDF viewer in drawer with "Download", "Send to artist", "Re-file" actions. [Source: gusto.com/taxes]

QuickBooks has the same pattern + **"eFile with IRS"** button.

**InkOS:** Tax forms tab under Payroll. Split sections: **Artist forms** (1099-NEC for contractors, W-2 for employees, W-9 on file check) and **Studio forms** (1099-K received from Dodo/Stripe, quarterly estimated, annual summary). Inline PDF viewer (react-pdf) in drawer. "Send secure link to artist" instead of email attachment (PII safety). Status chips: Draft / Ready to file / Filed / Delivered / Amended.

Encryption note: W-9 SSN fields must be encrypted at rest (Supabase pgcrypto + column-level RLS). Mask as `•••-••-1234` in UI; reveal requires re-auth + audit log entry. (Already covered in Sprint 12 hardening but Sprint 9 must stub the storage.)

### CSV export
Stripe's "Export" button opens a modal: Date range, Columns to include (multi-check), Format (CSV/JSON), Delivery (Download now / Email when ready). For >10k rows it queues + emails. [Source: dashboard.stripe.com/exports]

**InkOS:** Same pattern. Presets: "Payroll for accountant" (artist, period, gross, tax, net), "Commission detail" (every line), "IRS 1099 export". Export queued via BullMQ; email link when ready. Signed URL, 24h expiry.

---

## Part 4 — Tenant Billing

### Plan comparison table
Linear's pricing page has **3-column table with feature rows + checkmarks**, current plan highlighted with purple ring, "Upgrade" CTA per column. [Source: linear.app/pricing] Notion uses same pattern + **annual/monthly toggle**.

**InkOS:** 4 columns (Solo $29 / Studio $59 / Pro $99 / Enterprise $199). Rows: Artists included, Bookings/mo, Storage, AI design credits, Multi-location, SSO, Support SLA. Current plan highlighted with `--color-electric-purple` ring + "Current plan" badge. Grayed-out columns for downgrades (require cancel-survey).

### Usage meters with thresholds
Vercel's billing page shows **horizontal progress bars** per metered resource: Bandwidth, Function invocations, Build minutes. Bar fills green → amber at 75% → red at 90%. [Source: vercel.com/docs/billing]

Mercury uses **ring meters** on dashboard for card spend limits.

**InkOS:** Horizontal progress bars (Vercel model) on Billing page. Meters: Artists used (4 of 5), Bookings this month (234 of 500), AI credits (48 of 100), Storage (2.1 GB of 10 GB). Colors: `< 75%` neutral, `75–90%` amber, `> 90%` red. "Upgrade" inline CTA appears at 80%.

### Invoice history
Stripe's customer portal: **table with Date · Invoice # · Amount · Status (Paid/Open/Void) · PDF download icon**. [Source: stripe.com/docs/billing/customer/customer-portal] Mercury identical pattern.

**InkOS:** Copy Stripe customer portal verbatim. Columns: Date · Invoice # · Amount · Status · PDF. Click row → hosted invoice page (Dodo provides). "Download all (ZIP)" bulk action for accountant handoff.

### Payment method swap
Stripe portal: **Default card + "Add new card" + "Delete"** on non-default cards. Adding card uses Stripe Elements inline — no redirect. [Source: stripe.com/docs/payments/save-and-reuse]

**InkOS:** Dodo's equivalent hosted flow. UI: card brand icon · last 4 · exp · default badge · "Make default" / "Remove". "Add payment method" opens Dodo-hosted modal. Never touch card numbers directly (PCI scope zero).

### Cancel-with-retention
Notion and Linear both use a **3-step cancel flow**: Step 1 reason survey (radio: too expensive / missing features / switching / other), Step 2 **targeted retention offer** (50% off 3 months / downgrade to cheaper plan / pause subscription), Step 3 confirm. [Source: notion.so cancel flow]

Baremetrics data: 15–25% of cancels are saved by a good retention step. Worth building.

**InkOS:** Same 3-step pattern. Reason survey → conditional offer (too expensive → 30% for 3mo; missing feature → book call with Yash; switching → export-my-data + pause; other → direct cancel). Pause = 90 days free, read-only access, no data deletion. Confirm requires typing studio name.

---

## Part 5 — Admin Billing

### MRR dashboard
Baremetrics/ProfitWell set the bar: **Big hero number** (current MRR with MoM delta), then **line chart** (90-day MRR), then **breakdown cards** (New · Expansion · Contraction · Churn · Reactivation). Color scheme: green gains, red losses. [Source: baremetrics.com/demo, profitwell.com]

Mercury's account balance graph is the closest **UI reference** — clean line, hover shows tooltip with date + value, time-range pills (7D / 30D / 90D / YTD / All). [Source: mercury.com dashboard]

**InkOS:** Admin `/admin/billing` hero: MRR $XX,XXX (+12.4% MoM, green arrow). Below: 4 stat cards (New MRR, Expansion, Contraction, Churned). Below: line chart with Mercury-style time pills. Stacked bar option for "MRR by plan" breakdown.

### ARR projection
ProfitWell shows ARR = MRR × 12 with a **12-month projection** line extrapolated from last 3 months growth rate. Confidence band (light shaded area) shows ±10% range. [Source: profitwell.com metrics]

**InkOS:** Stat card "ARR (projected)" = current MRR × 12. Dotted-line extension on the main chart showing next 90 days projection. Small disclaimer "Based on trailing 90-day growth".

### Failed payments
Stripe's Dashboard has a **"Failed payments" table** with Reason code (insufficient funds, expired card, 3DS challenge), Retry count, Next retry, Dunning email status. Bulk "Retry all" action. [Source: dashboard.stripe.com]

**InkOS:** Table at `/admin/billing/failed-payments`. Columns: Studio · Amount · Reason · Attempt # · Next retry · Email sent? · Action (Retry now / Contact). Auto-retry schedule: 1d / 3d / 7d. After 3 fails → subscription state `past_due`; after 14 days → `suspended` (read-only).

### Churn cohorts
ProfitWell's **retention curve chart**: X-axis months since signup, Y-axis % retained, one line per cohort (Jan signups, Feb signups...). [Source: profitwell.com] Exposes whether retention is improving over time.

**InkOS:** Cohort heatmap table. Rows = signup month, columns = months since signup, cell = % retained (color-scaled green→red). Plus a single-chart overlay version for top 6 cohorts.

### LTV distribution
Baremetrics shows LTV as a **histogram + median marker**. Bins of $100 buckets. [Source: baremetrics.com/metrics] Most LTV dashboards just show an average, which hides a long tail.

**InkOS:** Histogram on `/admin/billing` → LTV tab. X-axis $ buckets, Y-axis count. Median and p90 markers as vertical dashed lines. Summary: Mean LTV, Median LTV, Payback period (months), LTV:CAC ratio (if CAC tracked).

---

## Part 6 — Three Replica Notes

### Replica 1: Stripe Payments drawer
Click any payment row → right-side drawer slides in (450px wide, `--color-ink-black` surface with subtle backdrop blur).

**Header:** Status chip (colored dot + text) · Amount XX-large monospace · Close X.
**Metadata grid (2-col):** ID · Date · Method (card brand + •••• 4242) · Client · Artist · Booking ID (linked).
**Timeline:** Vertical event list (Created → Auth → Captured → Succeeded / Refunded / Disputed), each with timestamp and actor.
**Actions bar (sticky footer):** Refund · Resend receipt · Copy ID · Dispute info (if applicable).
**Related records:** Booking link + Commission record link (expandable mini-cards).

Animation: drawer slides in 200ms ease-out, content fades 100ms after. Close on Escape or backdrop click.

### Replica 2: Gusto payroll approval
Single-page flow at `/payroll/runs/[id]/approve`:

**Top:** 5-step stepper (currently on step 3 "Approve").
**Summary card:** Pay period · Total gross · Total net · Total taxes · # of artists · Process date.
**Table:** Expandable rows per artist (collapsed shows Name + Net; expand shows line items).
**Warnings panel** (right rail, amber): "2 artists have unresolved disputes", "1 artist missing W-9 — block until uploaded".
**Approval gate (bottom):** Checkbox "I confirm these amounts are correct" + typed confirmation "Type APPROVE to continue" + primary CTA button (disabled until both).
**After approve:** Confetti-free success (tattoo studio owners are not Notion users) — just a clean toast "Payroll approved. Payouts scheduled for Friday." + redirect to run detail page in `processing` state.

### Replica 3: Mercury MRR graph
Hero card on `/admin/billing`:

**Top-left:** Label "MRR" (small caps, muted) · value `$47,320` (3xl, tabular-nums) · delta chip `+12.4% MoM` (green bg, rounded-full).
**Top-right:** Time-range pills (7D / 30D / **90D** / YTD / All) — active pill has `--color-electric-purple` ring.
**Chart:** Single line, 2px stroke, `--color-electric-purple` gradient fill fading to transparent (Mercury aesthetic). Smooth cubic-bezier, not jagged. Hover: crosshair + tooltip card with date + exact MRR.
**Below chart:** 4 stat cards in a grid — New MRR · Expansion · Contraction · Churned — each with mini-sparkline and MoM delta.
**Interactions:** Click-drag on chart to zoom time range. Double-click to reset. Click tooltip → opens drawer with that day's subscription events.

Library: Recharts (already in Stack A, Sprint 7 chose it) — NOT Chart.js (canvas-based, less composable).

---
